strategist.thesis: Bank of America (BAC) screens at opportunity 65.0 with an expectations gap of 15.0. Reality 59.0 reflects +15.9% TTM revenue growth, +36.2% operating margin and n/a ROIC; pricing 44.0 reflects a fair multiple and neutral price momentum. Macro fit for Financials in a Goldilocks regime is 53.0/100.

market_expectation.summary: Priced for stagnation or deterioration; the market is not paying for improvement.

what_market_misses: Reality (59.0) is running ahead of what is priced (44.0): an expectations gap of +15 pts.
Revenue growth is accelerating (+15.9% TTM, +3.7 pts) while the multiple has not re-rated.
Operating leverage is showing up in margins faster than in the valuation.
catalysts: Next quarterly report (roughly 90 days after the last filing on 2026-07-31)
risks: No engine-flagged risks; standard execution and macro risk apply.
thesis_break_conditions: Operating margin compresses more than 200 bps YoY (currently 36.2%)
Financials rotation score turns below -20 for two consecutive runs (currently -76)
Price closes >10% below its 200-day average with negative relative strength

llm.thesis: BAC is a high-quality earnings compounder being sold as a rotation casualty: TTM revenue +15.9% (accelerating from +12.2%), operating margin 36.2% (+729bps YoY), EPS +28% to $4.34, and a 3.7% reduction in diluted shares funded by $24.9B of buybacks — yet the stock trades at 11.6x earnings, below its own 5y median of 12x (43rd percentile) and at a PEG of 0.4. The engine's expectations gap of +15pts (reality 59 vs pricing 44) is consistent with a market paying nothing for the operating leverage already visible in the filings. The setup is technically stretched to the downside (RSI 24.8, -10.2% in a month, -13.6% from the 52w high) while price still holds 1.3% above a rising 200-day with a 50>200 structure — a mean-reversion window inside an intact uptrend. The principal caveat is that the engine's quality inputs are largely non-computable for a bank (ROIC n/a, net debt/EBITDA n/a, FCF is just operating cash flow distorted by balance-sheet flows, operating income is estimated), so the 'quality 67' and 'balance sheet strong' checks carry less information than they appear to. Sizing should respect a -76 Financials rotation score: this is a valuation-and-buyback thesis, not a flow thesis.
llm.fundamental_read: Growth is accelerating and margins are expanding sharply (+729bps YoY operating margin), with net income $33.7B on $121.1B revenue (27.8% net margin) and EPS growth (+28%) outrunning net income growth (+19.9%) purely on the -3.7% share count. Returns are bank-typical rather than exceptional: ROE 11.2%, ROA 0.96%, meaning the earnings power is leverage-driven and sensitive to rate path and credit costs, not a structurally high-ROIC franchise. Cash flow and leverage metrics in the dataset (FCF margin 78%, FCF conversion 2.8x, net debt $110B) are artifacts of bank accounting and should not be read as free cash generation or as a solvency signal. Shareholder yield of 6.3% is entirely buybacks in this dataset (dividends n/a), which is the clearest, most verifiable transmission of the earnings improvement to per-share value.
llm.technical_read: Primary trend is intact — price $56 sits 1.3% above a rising 200-day ($55.28) with 50>200 — but the intermediate trend has broken: close is well below the 20-day ($60.56) and 50-day ($61.75) with MACD histogram negative at -0.63. RSI14 at 24.8 is deeply oversold, a condition that in an uptrend historically resolves to the upside, but the 200-day at ~$55.3 is the line in the sand; a decisive weekly close below it converts this from a dip to a trend change. Risk/reward framework: buy zone $55-57, invalidation on a sustained close below ~$53 (roughly 4% under the 200dma), first resistance at the 50-day near $61.75.
llm.market_expectation: At 11.6x with a PEG of 0.4 and only +7.9% twelve-month return, the market is discounting that the current revenue and margin momentum is a peak-cycle artifact — i.e., that net interest income benefits fade with rate cuts, credit costs normalize, and 2026 earnings represent a high-water mark rather than a base. The -76 Financials rotation score says capital is actively leaving the sector for Technology (+73), so even good bank prints are not being rewarded with multiple expansion. In short: the market expects flat-to-down forward EPS ex-buyback and is unwilling to pay above the historical median multiple for cyclical, leverage-derived earnings.
what_market_misses: The buyback is doing quiet, mechanical work: $24.9B repurchased against a $392B market cap is a 6.3% yield that compounds EPS even if pre-tax earnings merely hold flat — the market is pricing the revenue line's cyclicality but not the per-share arithmetic.

Reality (59) is ahead of pricing (44) with revenue growth accelerating +3.7pts sequentially and the multiple actually sitting below its own 5y median — a multiple that has de-rated into improving fundamentals is the definition of an expectations gap.

The -76 sector rotation score is a crowding signal as much as a fundamental one; extreme negative rotation into a name that is still above its 200-day and oversold on RSI is historically a better entry than a worse one.

Regime probabilities are effectively uniform (Goldilocks 26.3 / Reflation 25.1 / Stagflation 23.7 / Contraction 24.9), meaning the 'Goldilocks' label carries almost no macro edge — the macro-fit score of 53 is closer to a coin flip than a tailwind, which cuts against both bulls and bears and pushes weight back onto valuation and buybacks.
Operating leverage of +729bps is unusually large for a bank of this size and, if even partially durable, is not reflected in a 43rd-percentile multiple.
catalysts: Next quarterly report (~90 days after the 2026-07-31 filing) — confirmation or refutation of the +15.9% revenue and 36.2% margin trajectory.
Annual capital plan / stress-test outcome enabling continued or expanded repurchase authorization, which sustains the 6.3% buyback yield.
Mean reversion from RSI 24.8 back toward the 50-day (~$61.75), roughly 10% from spot, with no fundamental change required.
Any reversal in the Financials rotation score from -76 toward neutral — the single largest swing factor for multiple expansion in this name.
Rate-path clarity: a steeper curve or slower-than-feared cuts would extend the net interest income tailwind embedded in the revenue acceleration.
risks: Credit normalization: provisions are not visible in this evidence set, and a bank at 0.96% ROA has limited cushion before credit costs materially dent EPS.
The revenue acceleration may be rate-driven and self-reversing; +15.9% growth for a universal bank is not a structural growth rate and should not be extrapolated.
Financials rotation at -76 means the stock can be fundamentally right and still de-rate for quarters as capital concentrates in Technology (+73).

Data quality: operating income is flagged as estimated, ROIC/incremental ROIC/net debt-to-EBITDA are n/a, and FCF is not meaningful — three of the twelve engine checks are uninformative for a bank, inflating apparent conviction.
Regulatory capital changes could force a reduction in the buyback, which is the core of the per-share thesis.
Momentum: price is below both the 20- and 50-day with negative MACD; oversold can persist and the 200-day is only 1.3% below spot.
thesis_break_conditions: Operating margin compresses more than 200bps YoY from 36.2%.
Buyback pace slows materially or share count stops shrinking (currently -3.7% YoY) — the per-share engine stalls.
Weekly close more than ~5% below the 200-day (~$52.5) with negative relative strength versus the S&P.
Provision expense or net charge-offs inflect sharply higher in the next two prints, driving net income growth negative.
Financials rotation stays below -50 for two or more consecutive runs while price also loses the 200-day.
second_order_beneficiaries: Private credit and alternative asset managers (Apollo, Ares, Blackstone, Blue Owl) — if regulatory capital constrains BAC's balance-sheet lending, non-bank lenders absorb the origination and earn the spread the bank cannot hold.

Core banking and payments infrastructure vendors (FIS, Fiserv, Jack Henry) plus cloud providers — a bank running 36% operating margins on accelerating revenue is proving that efficiency spend works, which sustains the technology budget that produced it.

Exchanges and market-structure operators (ICE, CME, Nasdaq) and interdealer brokers — BAC's markets revenue is their volume; the same rate volatility driving bank revenue drives their clearing and data fees.
Significant-risk-transfer and securitization arrangers, plus mortgage insurers — the mechanism by which a capital-constrained large bank keeps originating while shedding risk weight.
Money market fund complexes and custodians — the direct beneficiaries if deposit competition intensifies and cash sorts away from bank balance sheets, i.e., the hedge against the NII thesis.
Cybersecurity and identity/fraud vendors — a $3.5T asset institution's non-negotiable spend line regardless of the rate cycle.

epistemic_labels.statement: TTM revenue $121.1B, +15.9% YoY, accelerating from +12.2% the prior quarter.
Operating margin 36.2%, up 729bps YoY; EPS $4.34, +28.0%; net income $33.7B, +19.9%.
Diluted share count down 3.7% YoY with $24.9B of buybacks; buyback/shareholder yield 6.3%.
P/E 11.6x versus a 5y median of 12x (43rd percentile); PEG 0.4; earnings yield 8.6%.
Price $56, above a rising 200-day ($55.28) by 1.3%, below the 20-day and 50-day; RSI14 24.8; MACD histogram -0.63.
Financials sector rotation score -76 versus Technology +73.
ROE 11.2%, ROA 0.96%; ROIC, net debt/EBITDA and FCF growth are not computable from the data.
The market is pricing BAC's current earnings as peak-cycle and expects flat-to-declining forward EPS ex-buyback.
Financials will continue to lag as capital concentrates in Technology.
The reported FCF margin of 78% and FCF conversion of 2.8x are bank-accounting artifacts and should not be treated as free cash generation; likewise net debt of $110B is not a solvency signal.
The engine's 'quality 67' and 'balance sheet strong' checks are weakly supported because the underlying bank metrics (ROIC, leverage, FCF) are unavailable.
The revenue acceleration is substantially rate-driven rather than structural and is unlikely to persist at +15.9% beyond the current cycle.
Near-uniform regime probabilities mean the 'Goldilocks' label provides negligible macro edge, so valuation and buyback yield should dominate the decision.
RSI at 24.8 with price still above a rising 200-day marks a mean-reversion entry rather than the start of a trend change.
If Basel-style capital rules tighten, BAC's lending share migrates to private credit managers who earn the spread the bank cannot hold.
A reversal in the Financials rotation score from -76 toward neutral would be the largest single driver of multiple expansion in the next twelve months.
Continued 6% annual share count reduction could deliver positive per-share earnings growth even if pre-tax earnings decline modestly.
